surface.encoding: R,G = 16-bit W; B = signed depth: round((clamp(W - ground, -6, 24.6) + 6) / 0.12). Wet <=> depth > 0; table cells sit in (-2, 0]; buried ground <= -2.5.
surface.registration: texel i = refined sample 2i+1 = world (i + 0.5) * metresPerPixel
surface.idEncoding: R,G = 16-bit label; 0 none, else 1 + index into entities[]

season.runtime: The compiled W is the HIGH-WATER line (the wet season). The season only lowers it: level = W - amplitudeM * response * (1 - s) / 2 for the season scalar s in [-1, 1] (s = 1 wet season = the line, s = -1 dry season); wet <=> signedDepth + lift > 0. Nothing ever rises above the line (owner 2026-09-13).
season.encoding: DRAW-DOWN response 0..1 per texel: the dry season lowers this water by amplitudeM * response. Bodies: (levelM - drySeasonLevelM) / amplitudeM from the graph (marsh sheets 0.2, pools <= 0.07); perennial rivers band 1 0.07, bands 2-3 0.1; a SEASONAL reach to its bed (dry); the sea 0. A river's response ramps to its receiving body's over the last 60 m, so no step opens at a mouth.

tide.runtime: high water is the line: tideOffset = amplitude * (sin(phase) - 1) <= 0

flow.fetchEncoding: B = sqrt(fetch / fetchMaxM): the sea is fully developed (fetchMaxM); inland water reads the open water upwind along the prevailing wind (a diagonal march), seeded from the sea

klass.meaning: TYPE label over a SUPERSET of the wet area, not a wetness mask: what kind of water a cell belongs to, out to extPx past the shore and extRiseM above the high-water line. Wetness is the signed depth in water-surface.png B plus the season lift. A river through a body carries the body's class.
